title: Fix the bakery's daily city report

blocks.text: A bakery chain sends its city managers a report every evening: each city's revenue and number of customers, in alphabetical order, then how many sales were large. The managers have three complaints. The cities come in an order nobody can explain, the customer numbers are higher than the loyalty cards say, and on the quiet Sunday after a holiday the report wasn't sent at all.

`render(...)` already formats the report. Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/CityReport.java`: `revenueByCity`, `customersByCity` and `splitBySize`, each one stream ending in a collector. About six lines in total.

cases.says: on a busy day, revenue and customers are given per city, and the sales are split into large and small
the revenue map iterates its cities in alphabetical order
on a day with no large sale, the split still has an empty list of large sales, and the report renders
a customer who buys several times in a city is counted once there

origin.section: partitioningBy Always Has Both Keys; groupingBy Has Only the Keys It Saw

concepts: groupingBy's downstream collector decides what each group becomes (counting counts elements, mapping to a set keeps distinct values), and its map has no promised type or order unless a map factory such as TreeMap::new is given.
partitioningBy always has both the true and the false key; groupingBy by a predicate has only the keys some element mapped to, so a missing group reads as null.
